articles.title: Plans submitted for demolition of seven blocks on Lower Falinge Estate in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has submitted plans to demolish seven blocks on the Lower Falinge Estate to make way for 270 new homes, aiming to improve living conditions in the area.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has submitted plans to Rochdale Council for the demolition of seven blocks on the Lower Falinge Estate, with the aim of constructing 270 new homes. The blocks earmarked for demolition include Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zedburgh, and Vaynor, which have been identified as no longer providing safe and warm living conditions.

The proposed redevelopment will primarily take place on land adjacent to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road, with additional plots near Redcross Street also included in the plans. RBH has indicated that the new homes will be a mix of houses and flats, all available for social rent, and designed to meet modern energy efficiency standards.

The plans come after a previous attempt to demolish the blocks was halted by a legal challenge from residents, who argued that there was no clear regeneration plan following the demolition. However, RBH has now provided a detailed regeneration strategy, which includes creating new landscaping, public open spaces, and safer streets, as well as improved walking routes into Rochdale town centre.

One resident, Andy Roche, who currently occupies Zedburgh, expressed distress over the plans, stating that he feels the needs of residents have not been adequately considered. Despite being offered alternative housing options, he claims none meet his current living standards. RBH has stated that they have engaged with local residents and stakeholders to ensure the new homes reflect community priorities.

evidence_sources.captured_text: The major redevelopment scheme for a 'doomed' housing estate in Rochdale - Manchester Evening News ‌ ‌ Skip to main content Manchester Evening News: Number one for news, opinion, sport & celebrity news The major redevelopment scheme for a 'doomed' housing estate in Rochdale The western part of the Lower Falinge Estate has been earmarked for demolition for years View 4 Images Flats in the Lower Falinge estate in Rochdale - earmarked for more demolition (Image: Jake Lindley / Manchester Evening News) Add to preferred sources Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 06:11, 21 Oct 2026 Seven blocks on Rochdale’s Lower Falinge estate are set to be demolished to make way for 270 new homes. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have officially submitted plans to the council to bulldoze Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zedburgh and Vaynor. Once they are demolished RBH would start work on building a mixture of homes and flats, all available for social rent. The majority of the 270 homes would go on the land due to be bulldozed – next to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road to the west. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter ‌ There are plots east of the giant estate, near to Redcross Street, that would also be built on under the proposals. RBH bought up the land to the east in recent years, just next to St Mary’s Gate. The proposals, if approved by Rochdale council , also intend to create new landscaping, public open spaces, safer streets, and new walking routes into the town centre. View 4 Images CGIs of how the new homes planned for Lower Falinge in Rochdale could look (Image: RBH) RBH says they have to demolish the seven remaining blocks because they are at the end of their life and no longer provide safe, warm homes. Six of the blocks have been empty for years. Only Zedburgh remains occupied by Andy Roche and his partner . ‌ When RBH’s initial vision was revealed two months ago, Andy said: “Obviously it’s extremely distressing for me because it involves being forced out of my home. I am not happy about RBH’s proposals, but I’m not sure how to put it into words. “I’m still processing it. I don’t believe they have listened to the residents of the estate at all. View 4 Images Andy Roche, sitting outside within the empty Lower Falinge estate blocks (Image: Jake Lindley / Manchester Evening News) “My partner is also distraught. We are both autistic and this eviction is making us both really ill.” ‌ So many tenants have upped sticks and moved on, but for Andy this estate has everything he wants. He has been offered multiple different housing options by RBH, but none of them have lived up to what he currently has, he claims. Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source The pair are part of the campaign group trying to stop demolition. Campaigners successfully stopped RBH’s application to demolish the blocks last year with a legal challenge . Their winning argument in preventing demolition was that the proposal lacked a future regeneration plan after the blocks got levelled. But now RBH has provided one. ‌ View 4 Images CGIs of how the new homes planned for Lower Falinge in Rochdale could look (Image: RBH) RBH says the new homes ‘will be modern and energy efficient’, designed to meet the Future Homes Standard. The developers claim this will make the homes warmer and more comfortable throughout the year; cost less to heat and run; reduce carbon emissions; provide homes for people at different stages of life; and be accessible and adaptable for changing needs. Hannah Fleming, RBH Director of Regeneration and Asset Improvement, said: “We want to say thank you to everyone who has shared their views with us before we submitted this application. We’ve spoken to residents, businesses, community groups, and local stakeholders. “Our aim is to build new homes that current and future customers will be proud to live in and strengthen the bonds that already exist within the local community in Lower Falinge and Rochdale town centre.
